Libya’s Electric Utilities Sector Disrupted by Respiratory Illness Outbreak

A widespread outbreak of acute respiratory illness has hit Libya’s electric utilities industry, causing operational disruptions and workforce shortages at major sites across the country, industry sources said Monday. The situation remains ongoing, with the General Electricity Co of Libya among the companies most affected.

According to a statement from the Libyan Electrical Workers Union, more than 180 employees across power generation and grid maintenance facilities have reported symptoms or have been quarantined in the past week. The most significant impact has been reported at the Tajoura and Zawiya power stations, where workforce availability has dropped by nearly 20 percent.

General Electricity Co of Libya said in a brief update that “staffing constraints are affecting daily operations. Some maintenance and grid repair work has been postponed as a precautionary measure.” Emergency teams have been dispatched to critical locations to maintain supply, but rolling blackouts have been reported in several districts of Tripoli and Misrata as a result.

“We are working closely with health authorities and taking all possible steps to contain the outbreak and protect our employees,” said Khaled al-Barassi, a company spokesperson. “However, if cases continue to rise, further service interruptions cannot be ruled out.”

Industry analyst Nasser Tumi noted, “The sector’s already limited technical workforce is under extreme strain. Prolonged absenteeism could impact electricity production and distribution in the short term.”

The Libyan Electrical Services Association has urged all utilities to enhance workplace hygiene protocols and provide protective equipment. The full impact of the outbreak is still unfolding, with ongoing assessments as companies monitor infection rates and manage resources.
